title: Babies are placed on the back for every sleep, CDC's safe-sleep page says
summary: CDC says to place a baby on the back for all sleep times, both naps and night, to reduce the risk of sleep-related infant death.
body: CDC's safe-sleep page says caregivers can lower the risk of sleep-related infant deaths, including sudden infant death syndrome and accidental suffocation. The first action it lists is to place the baby on the back for every sleep, naps and night. The page says CDC supports the 2022 recommendations of the American Academy of Pediatrics. NICHD's Safe to Sleep campaign is the US public campaign built around that back-sleep practice. This is the US page's instruction. It is not an order written for one baby, and another country's campaign can differ in the details around it.

sources.title: Providing Care for Babies to Sleep Safely
